Assistant: Well, that's a great question! There are many ways to give back, but one of the most rewarding is through mentorship programs. You can share your experiences and knowledge with others who are just starting out. What kind of field are you in?
User: I'm actually in education, or at least that's where my heart is. I love helping students navigate their academic and professional journeys.
Assistant: That's amazing! Education is such a vital field. Have you considered working with a specific age group or demographic? For example, high school students or young adults in college?
User: Yeah, I think I'd like to work with college students. They're at such a pivotal point in their lives, trying to figure out their futures. I feel like I could really make a difference there.
Assistant: Absolutely! College students often need guidance and support as they navigate their academic and professional paths. There are many organizations that offer mentorship programs for college students. Have you looked into any of those?
User: Actually, I've been looking into a few programs, but I haven't committed to anything yet. I want to make sure I find the right fit.
Assistant: That's a great approach. It's essential to find a program that aligns with your values and goals. Can you tell me more about what you're looking for in a mentorship program?
User: Well, I'd love to work with a program that allows me to build meaningful relationships with students and provide them with individualized support. I also want to be part of a community that values education and personal growth.
Assistant: I think I can help you with that. There are many universities that offer mentorship programs that might fit what you're looking for. Have you considered reaching out to any local universities to see what opportunities they have available?
User: Actually, I've been volunteering at the University of New Mexico's mentorship program, guiding current students through their academic and professional journeys. It's been a really rewarding experience so far.
Assistant: That's fantastic! The University of New Mexico has a great reputation for its mentorship programs. What's been the most rewarding part of your experience so far? Is there a particular student or success story that stands out to you?
User: Oh, definitely! There's one student who was struggling to find her place in the world, and through our conversations, she discovered a passion for environmental science. It's been amazing to see her grow and develop as a person.
Assistant: That's incredible! It's stories like those that remind us of the impact we can have on others. What do you think is the most important quality for a mentor to have, and how do you embody that in your own mentorship style?
User: I think the most important quality is empathy. As a mentor, you need to be able to understand and relate to your mentees' struggles and concerns. I try to create a safe and non-judgmental space for my students to share their thoughts and feelings.
Assistant: I couldn't agree more. Empathy is essential for building trust and rapport with your mentees. It sounds like you're doing some amazing work at the University of New Mexico. What are your long-term goals for your mentorship work, and how do you see yourself continuing to make an impact in the lives of your students?
User: I'm really worried about finding a job. I've applied to so many places, but I haven't heard back from any of them yet.
Assistant: That's tough. How long have you been looking?
User: About a month now.
Assistant: That's not too bad. It can take a while to hear back from places. Have you tried following up with any of them?
User: Yeah, I've sent a few follow-up emails, but I still haven't heard anything.
Assistant: Well, don't give up hope. I'm sure you'll find something eventually. Have you considered reaching out to any alumni from your college?
User: No, I haven't really thought about that. Do you think that would be helpful?
Assistant: Definitely. Alumni are often willing to help out recent graduates, and they might be able to provide some job leads or advice.
User: That's a good idea. I'll have to look into that.
Assistant: And don't forget to keep applying to job postings. You never know when something might come up.
User: Thanks for the advice. I really appreciate it.
Assistant: No problem. Hey, speaking of jobs, do you remember that time in college when we both applied for the same position and ended up interviewing on the same day?
User: Yes, I remember that. And then we found out we both got rejected.
Assistant: Yeah, that was a bummer. But hey, it all worked out in the end.
User: Yeah, I guess so. Hopefully it will this time, too.

c79-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: Stay connected. Rely on us for support. The Ball State University Alumni Association is nearly 190,000 strong—this incredible network is here for you. Discover the many ways you can get involved.
Find a group of alumni who live near you and share your interests and love for Ball State.
Shop for merchandise, buy a license plate, and let us know what’s going on with you.
Advance your career, save money on insurance, and connect with fellow alumni.
Staff and volunteer members of our Alumni Council work together to guide and lead your Alumni Association.
The Alumni Association recognizes the university's top volunteers, and paves the way for the next generation of Cardinals.
There’s nothing better than getting together with fellow alumni—at home, in a new city, or on campus. Join the fun!
Visit our online magazine and learn more about what our students, alumni, and faculty are up to. Based on the passage above, How can I become involved in advancing my career and connecting with other alumni?
Assistant: You can become involved in advancing your career and connecting with other alumni by joining the Ball State University Alumni Association. They offer career advancement opportunities and connections with other alumni.
User: That sounds great! Could you please guide me on how to find a group of alumni who live near me and share my interests and love for Ball State?
Assistant: Sure! To find a group of alumni who live near you and share your interests and love for Ball State, you can visit the Ball State University Alumni Association website and click on the "Connect" tab. Under the "Get Involved" section, click on "Alumni Groups" and you can search for alumni groups by location and interest. You can also contact the Alumni Association directly for assistance in finding a group that best fits your interests and location.
User: Living and working in Southern California 2,446 miles from the University of North Florida campus, Jenna LeMaster was curious about whether there were any fellow Ospreys in the area, so she logged on to the professional networking site LinkedIn and searched. To her surprise, she found more than 130.
“I’ve been out of school for almost eight years and have yet to utilize the Alumni Association’s benefits, so I thought if there are that many people living out here, I bet they would be just as excited to leverage the Osprey community for support, whether it be [making] a new friend with Florida roots or a business contact,” she said.
So LeMaster contacted fellow alumni in the area and enlisted them to join her in petitioning UNF’s Alumni Association to establish an alumni chapter in the Southern California/Los Angeles area.
The association’s board of directors approved the chapter at its January meeting, and UNF now has two alumni clubs – one in California and one in New York. The association is talking with alumni in Washington, D.C., about forming a club and with alumni in Atlanta about reforming their club as well.
It may seem odd that UNF would start alumni clubs in Los Angeles and New York City, but consider this: About two dozen universities from outside Florida have active alumni clubs in Jacksonville, including the University of Southern California, which is just a short drive from where LeMaster works as a marketing director in Hermosa Beach. Washington State, Syracuse, Penn State, Kentucky and Notre Dame all have clubs in UNF’s shadow. Even the Harvard Business School has an alumni club in Jacksonville.
Alumni clubs provide graduates with an opportunity to reconnect with their alma mater and network with other alumni. Many clubs offer something for all age groups, whether participants are interested in social or cultural events, athletics, philanthropy or making business contacts. They’re great for networking.
The Georgia Tech club, for example, serves as a forum for alumni, parents, family and friends of Georgia Tech to socialize, volunteer and even recruit and interview prospective students, according to its Web site. Older colleges and universities with large alumni bases have formed clubs throughout the country. For example, Auburn University, which was chartered in 1856, has 98 alumni clubs in 24 states. Its Jacksonville club has 385 members.
UNF, which opened for classes in 1972, only has 60,239 alumni spread throughout the United States, though most live in Florida and nearly half remain on the First Coast.
Kerry N. User: What role can alumni associations and networks play in supporting universities, and how can universities cultivate meaningful relationships with their graduates over time?
Assistant: Alumni associations and networks can play a vital role in supporting universities in several ways. Firstly, they can help with fundraising efforts by connecting with alumni who are willing to donate to their alma mater. These associations can also help with recruitment efforts by connecting current students with alumni who can serve as mentors, offer job opportunities, and make valuable introductions. Additionally, alumni networks can serve as ambassadors for the university, promoting its values and achievements to a wider audience.

To cultivate meaningful relationships with their alumni, universities should create opportunities for engagement beyond graduation. This includes offering ways for alumni to reconnect with one another, as well as with faculty and staff members. Universities should also actively seek input and feedback from their alumni regarding their experiences as students and how the university can improve its offerings for future students. Creating a robust online presence and leveraging social media can also help universities stay connected with their alumni communities. Finally, hosting events and activities that offer relevant programming and opportunities for networking can help build and maintain strong relationships between alumni and their alma mater.

Additionally, alumni associations can help universities by organizing events and initiatives that bring alumni and industry leaders together to discuss potential partnerships and collaborations. They can also provide input and guidance on what types of partnerships would be most beneficial for both the university and the partner organization. Therefore, universities can leverage their alumni networks to establish strategic partnerships that can lead to new opportunities for research, funding, and collaboration with other institutions.

Overall, universities recognize the importance of maintaining strong relationships with their alumni members and often provide various benefits to encourage alumni engagement and support.

Allie Kelly and Cameron Laukaitis used to call the volleyball and basketball courts their home, but now they’re making an impact in the rowing realm.
The Kirkland residents along with several other Sammamish Rowing Association athletes recently signed their letters of intent to compete in college. Their schools of choice are University of Texas at Austin (Kelly), Lehigh University (Laukaitis), Oregon State University (Mary Kirchoff and Kathryn Clemens) and Southern Methodist University (Faith Epp).
It’s a family rowing affair for Kelly, whose dad competed at Stanford University and now her mom, sister and brother also participate in the sport. Allie, who attends The Overlake School in Redmond, played school and club volleyball for nine years before she sustained a concussion. She returned to the sport after healing, but no longer had the passion for volleyball, she said. And along came rowing.
Allie knew from the start that she would soon be bonding with the other girls in their quest for success. After the first two weeks, she was sore everywhere, she laughed, and she persevered to keep on track.
She’s ready to become part of the “sisterhood” on her college team, which took third place at the NCAA championships last season. It’s a program on the rise and she’d like to be a part of its future success, she said.
Juanita’s Laukaitis played basketball for seven years, but when she entered high school, she wanted to test the proverbial waters and try something new. Her dad was an SRA member and pointed her toward rowing.
Laukaitis’s confidence level has risen through rowing, and like Kelly, she enjoys going that extra adrenaline-filled mile to achieve stellar results.
Most of her dad’s family is from back east and the rower is ready to tackle the Pennsylvania waters with her new school. During her visit to Lehigh, she envisioned personal connections on tap with her future teammates she met at the welcoming school.

The Rapids will continue the tradition of hosting their annual 4thFest contest on Independence Day. Colorado will face the New England Revolution on Thursday, July 4 (7:00 PM). The Rapids have an all-time record of 14-5-3 in July 4 contests.
With expansion side FC Cincinnati joining MLS this season, the Rapids will play all Eastern Conference teams once, six at home (DC, CLB, CIN, NE, NYC, MTL) and six on the road (ORL, CHI, ATL, PHI, NYRB, TOR), and all Western Conference teams twice (home and away).
The Rapids will be featured in two nationally televised matches - the first on the road at Dallas on Mar. 23 and the second at home against LAFC on Jun. 8. All non-nationally televised games will be aired locally on Altitude TV, as well as over the airwaves on Altitude 92.5 FM.
Individual tickets for the 2019 Colorado Rapids season will be available for purchase starting Wednesday, January 9 at 10 a.m. MT on AltitudeTickets.com . Colorado Rapids Full Season Ticket Members will have the opportunity to purchase additional tickets for the 2019 home season starting today.

c105-m1.summary: The user is a sports enthusiast and a tech professional.
c105-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: If you love sports and narrow development focus is too boring for you, then you have a great chance to combine your lifestyle and professional career here. As Sportlyzer is growing, you will have a great chance to be part of the option program and grow into the tech lead or CTO of Sportlyzer.
Sportlyzer is an Estonian startup, developing team management and player development software for youth sports clubs. Sports clubs can bring all of their staff and players to Sportlyzer, organize their calendars, collect training fees, track players’ progress, and simplify all related communication. The product is ready and used by hundreds of paying sports clubs from 40+ countries.
Take over and continue full stack development and maintenance of Sportlyzer’s backend and frontend.
Participate in product strategy and design brainstorms.
Gulp scripts (build system), wkhtmltopdf (generating invoices).
Agile development and lean startup practices.
Monitoring platform performance and user activity.
Very good in reading and understanding existing code.
Experience with a wide variety of testing techniques.
Flexible to adapt to changing requirements.
Ability to manage time to meet deadlines and milestones.
Positive, hardworking and a great team player.
Addictions: You love sports? – Cool, then we share your addiction! With us you can combine your professional career and lifestyle.
Salary and options: It depends on how good you are – we’ll talk about it!
Location: Office in the centre of Tartu, Estonia (we expect you to be in Tartu full time).
Working languages: English (compulsory), Estonian (optional).
To get started, simply send us your CV and links to anything you have built.
Sportlyzer is an award-winning team and training management software for youth and amateur sports. See more about the software from our website. How does Sportlyzer cater to the needs of youth sports clubs worldwide, and what is the working language requirement for this position?
Assistant: Sportlyzer caters to the needs of youth sports clubs worldwide by providing team management and player development software. The software helps to organize calendars, collect training fees, track players' progress, and simplify communication for sports clubs. The working language requirement for this position is English (compulsory), with Estonian being optional.
User: That sounds great! Can you please confirm if the position requires experience with both frontend and backend development? Also, can you provide more information on the product strategy and design brainstorms?
Assistant: Yes, the position requires experience with both frontend and backend development. As for the product strategy and design brainstorms, this means you will be able to participate in discussions regarding the long-term vision for the product and also help to come up with new product features to improve the user experience. You will work closely with the product team to come up with ideas for new features and enhancements to existing ones, and provide feedback on how to improve the product design to make it more effective and user-friendly. Additionally, you might also need to conduct research and analysis to understand the needs and preferences of the user base, keeping the company's goals and objectives in mind.
User: Can you please provide more information on the testing techniques that are required for this position? Also, can you share some examples of the types of deadlines and milestones I will be expected to meet?
Assistant: As a Full Stack Developer at Sportlyzer, you will be required to have experience with a wide variety of testing techniques. Some of the essential techniques you should be familiar with include automated testing, manual testing, performance testing, regression testing, and acceptance testing. Regarding deadlines and milestones, you will be expected to manage your time effectively to ensure the timely delivery of your work. You'll have to work with your team and participate in agile development processes throughout the development lifecycle. You might be asked to set up specific time frames for completing tasks, work on specific milestones to meet project goals or complete a list of programming activities within a specified period. Some examples of the deadlines and milestones include completing the integration of a new feature within a few weeks, meeting with the product team to discuss product upgrades within two weeks, and delivering finished code for testing within a specific time period. You should be able to prioritize your workload to ensure that you meet these deadlines and milestones.
User: Hello, I recently purchased the Rico Industries NFL Mens Embossed Leather Trifold Wallet and it's amazing! The quality is top-notch and the engraved design looks even better in person. I'm really happy with my purchase!
Assistant: That's great to hear! The Rico Industries NFL Mens Embossed Leather Trifold Wallet is indeed a fantastic choice. By the way, I came across another product you might like - the NFL Deep Slant Micro Raschel Throw. It's a cozy and stylish throw blanket. Would you be interested in it?
User: Thanks for the recommendation, but I've actually seen the NFL Deep Slant Micro Raschel Throw before. So, I'll pass on it.
Assistant: Alright, no problem. How about the CAP Barbell Olympic 2-Inch Solid Chrome Bar? It's a sturdy and well-made barbell. I can provide more details if you're interested.
User: Thanks for the suggestion, but I'm already familiar with the CAP Barbell Olympic 2-Inch Solid Chrome Bar as well. I've seen similar sports equipment before, so I'll have to decline.
Assistant: Understood. In that case, I have another recommendation for you. Have you considered the Can Can Concealment Hip Hugger Classic Woman's Holster? It's a popular choice for concealed carry. Let me provide you with more information.
User: I'm not sure yet. Can you give me more details about the sports holster?
Assistant: Absolutely! The Can Can Concealment Hip Hugger Classic Woman's Holster is an amazing product. It offers a comfortable fit and provides effective concealed carry. Many customers have praised its performance and how well it conceals. It's definitely worth considering!
User: Alright, I'll accept your recommendation. Thank you for the detailed information.
Assistant: You're welcome! If you need any more recommendations or have any other questions, feel free to ask.
User: Thank you for your help, but I think I'm good for now. I really appreciate your assistance!
Assistant: Not a problem at all! I'm glad I could assist you. If you ever need further assistance in the future, don't hesitate to reach out. Have a great day!
User: You too! Goodbye.
Assistant: Goodbye and take care!
